study.title: Multispectral image fusion and attention-driven deep learning for precision weed segmentation and classification in UAV-based agricultural monitoring
study.short_title: Sorghum weed: PCCSAN-DenseNet121 U-Net mIoU 0.9656, 2.1M params, RTX 4090

segmentation.domain: Crop/weed segmentation and classification in UAV multispectral sorghum imagery (precision agriculture, site-specific herbicide application); framework = PCCSAN-based DenseNet121 U-Net with U-MAFT multispectral fusion (green/red/red-edge/NIR), SNSFD shearlet feature decomposition, and Willow Catkin (WCO) population optimization
models_tested: PCCSAN-based DenseNet121 U-Net + U-MAFT + SNSFD + WCO (proposed)
segmentation.best_model: Proposed PCCSAN-based DenseNet121 U-Net: 5-fold CV mean IoU 96.56% +- 0.13 (best; class IoU background 99.55, crop 91.8, weed 93.32) with 2.1M params, 55.6 GFLOPs, ~0.000621 s/image on RTX 4090 vs best baseline mIoU 88.1 (U-Net-CRF) / 87.42 (MESA-Net)

dataset.name: Author-collected UAV multispectral dataset at the University of Queensland Gatton Research Farm (maize and sorghum plots; red-loamy soil, ridge-furrow, natural weed mixtures). DJI Phantom 3 Pro + MicaSense RedEdge camera, 5 spectral bands (blue 440 nm, green 560 nm, red 680 nm, red-edge 750 nm, NIR 710 nm), 2 m flight AGL at 1 m/s, GSD ~1.2 cm/px; 80%/70% forward/side overlap; radiometric calibration pre/post flight
dataset.note: 1240 images split spatially-straitified 70/15/15 (trace 868, validation 186, test 186). Three semantic classes: background/crop/weed (annotation via CVAT, 3 expert agronomists, inter-annotator agreement kappa 0.87 on 150-image subset; pixel distribution ~55% background / 28% crop / 17% weed). Dataset is author-collected, not publicly released; experimental setup on NVIDIA RTX 4090, PyTorch, 100 epochs, batch 2, WCO optimizer (no gradient-based optimizer), CE loss, dropout 0.3.

segmentation.backbone: PCCSAN (Patch Convolution + Catkin Sheaf Attention Network) ahead of a DenseNet121 encoder with a U-Net decoder: patch-based convolution (5x5xS patches, stride 1, no pooling) -> SheafAN attention message-passing over an 8-connected patch graph (transport matrices, spectral constraints) -> DenseNet121 encoder -> U-Net decoder -> 512x512x3 output. Multispectral input bands fused by U-MAFT (modified Swin-hierarchical encoder, dual-branch local-window + global downsampled attention). SNSFD (non-subsampled shearlet, 3 scales, directional partitions {8,8,16}, top-20% coefficients) adds channels. Full pipeline optimized by WCO (population-based, drift-and-adhesion), NOT Adam/SGD

mIoU.quote: The proposed method received an average Mean IoU of 96.56% ... the highest IoU scores of 99.55% for the background, 91.8% for the crops, and 93.32% for the weeds, leading to a Mean IoU of 96.56%
mIoU.ambiguity: 5-fold cross-validation mean over 186-image test subsets, CI 96.56 +- 0.13. Class-wise IoU: background 0.9955, crop 0.918, weed 0.9332. RGB-input-only ablation mIoU 0.9277 (~4-5% gain credited to 5-band multispectral fusion). Based on author-collected sorghum dataset.

F1.quote: The F1 score, the composite measure of precision and recall, was 98.76%
F1.ambiguity: 5-fold CV mean F1 = 98.76% (CI +- 0.03); definition in Eq. 38 is the two-term Precision/Recall harmonic mean. Abstract states 98.76% F1; precision 98.9% and recall 99.5% (fold-mean 98.89/99.52).

Dice.ambiguity: Regular Dice not reported; BOUNDARY Dice reported at 92.4% for the full model (Tables 9-10).

PA.quote: the proposed weed segmentation and classification framework shows a marked superiority over current models, with the overall accuracy of 98.8% being a notable achievement
PA.ambiguity: Overall/pixel accuracy 98.8% reported against baselines (ResNet101-v 97.2%, DenseNet-169 98.56%, SSU-Net 90.47%, Tuned-DNN 90.5%, YOLOv5 64.8%); definition in Eq. 35 (TP+TN)/(TP+TN+FP+FN).

weed_F1.ambiguity: Per-class F1 not reported; per-class weed IoU 0.9332 reported.

crop_F1.ambiguity: Per-class F1 not reported; per-class crop IoU 0.918 reported.

edge.device: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 GPU (desktop); no embedded/edge deployment - future work explicitly targets 'lightweight model architectures suitable for real-time inference on UAVs'
edge.framework: PyTorch (WCO population-based optimizer, no gradient-based optimizer)

fps.quote: the inference time is 0.000621 s per image per instance
fps.ambiguity: DERIVED as 1000/0.62 ms. edge.reported=false (desktop RTX 4090). Implausibly high for 512x512 semantic segmentation and inconsistent with the 55.6 GFLOPs figure on the same hardware - flagged as likely under-reported pipeline cost; do not use as an edge-rate reference.

latency_ms.quote: only takes 2.1 million parameters, and the inference time is 0.000621 s per image per instance, which is faster and more compact than all models compared
latency_ms.ambiguity: Paper reports ~0.000621 s (Section 4.5/conclusion) and 0.62 ms (Table 7) per image on RTX 4090 - a desktop measurement and an implausibly small value for 512x512 segmentation; likely reflects single-image/instance timing excluding full pipeline. edge.reported=false.

params_M.quote: The proposed model proves to be very efficient, as it only takes 2.1 million parameters
params_M.ambiguity: Structural computational metric. Table 6 total 2.1M vs Table 7 module breakdown (U-MAFT+SNSFD 1.35 + PatchConv 0.3 + DenseNet121 encoder 0.6 + U-Net decoder 0.25 + SheafAN 0.1 + TWVF 0.01 = ~2.6M) - internal inconsistency flagged. Baselines: MESA-Net 6.74M, SSU-Net 2.5M, MaxViT 22.08M.

gflops.ambiguity: Structural computational metric. 55.6 GFLOPs total pipeline (U-MAFT 33G + SNSFD 36.5G combination row; module-level FLOPs: PatchConv 8.7G, DenseNet121 12.2G, U-Net decoder 6.1G, SheafAN 3G, TWVF 0.2G). Model size 18.5 MB.

issues: edge.reported=false: everything measured on desktop RTX 4090; no edge/embedded deployment, and the future-work section explicitly calls for 'lightweight model architectures suitable for real-time inference on UAVs'. Reported latency 0.62 ms / ~1600 FPS is implausible for 512x512 segmentation (inconsistent with 55.6 GFLOPs on the same GPU) - flagged in the edge block.

Screening was PROVISIONAL_FULLTEXT_ELIGIBILITY / EXC-06 (no abstract, no retrievable results at screening time); the full text contains a complete quantitative evaluation (5-fold CV mIoU 96.56% +- 0.13 - confirmed quantitative results) so the record is created, consistent with the SCI-000440 precedent.

Author-collected dataset (maize + sorghum, Gatton Research Farm, DJI Phantom 3 Pro + MicaSense RedEdge, 2 m AGL, ~1.2 cm/px, 1240 images), not public; only sorghum tested, acknowledged as limiting generalization.
Internal inconsistency: total params 2.1M (Table 6/conclusion) vs ~2.6M summed from the Table 7 module breakdown.

5-band multispectral fusion (vs RGB) adds ~4-5% mIoU (RGB-only 92.77% vs full U-MAFT 96.56%); WCO optimizer (96.56 mIoU, 85 epochs to 52 convergence epochs) vs Adam 94.78 / SGD 91.85 / PSO 93.92 / ACO 94.10 mIoU.

Class-wise IoU: background 99.55 / crop 91.8 / weed 93.32; some figures (crop 91.8, weed 93.32) exceed realistic crop-weed discrimination reported elsewhere in the corpus, but are recorded faithfully.
